correctness.rationale: For n not divisible by three the kernel recurrence forces zero; for n=3m it yields precisely four period-three XOR masks. Fixed-weight pair collisions require m selected bits on a 2m-coordinate support; triple collisions fix class weights (2m-w,w-m,w-m); all-four collisions require half of each class. Anchored combinatorial counts divided by orientation/anchor multiplicities give M_1 through M_4; binomial inversion gives B_1 through B_4 and exact capacity and thresholds. Replayed direct enumeration covers every (n,w) through n=18 (189 slices, 524286 input evaluations) and exact arithmetic all weights through n=240; finite checks are not substituted for proof. No unresolved critical lemma or normalization remains.

originality.rationale: The checked primary finite-cellular-automaton literature supplies unrestricted reversibility (Rule 150 invertible when 3 does not divide ring length), inverses in the reversible regime, and additive-automaton dynamical decision procedures. A related complete Rule 150 result counts unrestricted preimages after quotienting rotations, whereas the present theorem counts indexed output fibers restricted to each source Hamming sphere, giving all four list-size populations. Full text of the closest cyclic integer-weighted-read result was inspected: its observation is the ordered vector of integer window sums, not XOR Rule 150, hence its constant-weight capacity does not imply this result. Search of source claims and aliases found no identified covering theorem; general coset-weight theory is a material unresolved historical-priority risk, not treated as disproved.
residual_risks: The Hamming-weight enumerator of cosets of a linear binary code is a standard general object; an earlier all-purpose formula might imply this four-element kernel specialization without mentioning Rule 150.
No search result or indexed repository can prove priority over every unpublished, historical or unindexed conference result.
The reviewed closest published-finding corpus and primary texts cover the named comparisons, but exhaustive screening of all coding-theory literature was not possible.

value.rationale: Hamming-weight constraints are natural in constant-composition communication and data acquisition. The claimed all-size exact output distinguishability and complete inverse-list census have a direct operational interpretation as the zero-error codebook size and reconstruction list-size distribution for a fixed-composition Rule 150 parity sensor. Unlike the elementary unrestricted four-preimage bound, the theorem gives a sharp injectivity transition at densities one-third and two-thirds and locates genuine threefold versus fourfold collisions. This answers a natural exact reconstruction invariant without asserting a new general coding theorem.
